- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67); increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 days if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (bearish), model often misses bottoming; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for next 3–5 days to avoid underestimation.
